title: st start realises from canon without comparing against the disk, so an unhydrated thread gets a smaller copy at the authoritative path
body:
## Summary

`intent st start` realises a thread's files from canon **without comparing what it is about to write against what is on disk.** On a thread whose canon is not fully hydrated, it writes a materially smaller copy at the canonical path while the complete original stays tracked elsewhere -- **two directories, and the incomplete one looks authoritative.**

Reported by laksa-vc; laksa-dc hit it and stopped mid-verb with nothing committed. Measured on Laksa's ST0106: the realised copy was **9493 bytes against the original's 14789**, missing `design.md`, `impl.md` and `tasks.md` entirely plus 58 lines of hand prose in `acceptance.md`. The tracked original was unmodified. Canon `wip`, `steel_threads.md` and `todo.md` were all updated correctly and thread-only.

**The verb is not corrupting.** It writes what canon has, and canon had less than the disk did because the thread predates full hydration. That is the point: **a lifecycle verb that silently writes less than the tree already held is a missing guard whatever the intended flow is.**

## The two losses are different defects, and treating them as one destroys the second

Measured against this estate's canon:

| file | kind |
| --- | --- |
| `design.md` / `impl.md` / `tasks.md` | **attachment** |
| `acceptance.md` / `info.md` | **generated view** |

- **The three missing files are a HYDRATION GAP.** Canon has less than disk. The route back is getting the disk content into canon, then realising.
- **The 58 lines in `acceptance.md` are hand prose in a GENERATED VIEW**, which D02 forbids and which any regeneration was always going to discard. **`st start` did not cause that; it revealed it.** Attaching `acceptance.md` to preserve the prose would create an authored file where the model says there is a generated one -- trading a visible loss for a silent model violation. That prose needs a home that survives: the criterion/AT notes it describes, which are canon, or `design.md` as an attachment.

## `hydrate` is NOT the completion

`intent st hydrate` is *"Add a steel thread to .intentfiles and WRITE ITS FILES"* -- canon to disk. On an impoverished canon it re-realises the same impoverished copy. Recorded because it is the plausible-looking remedy and it is wrong.

## The remedy is already derived in this codebase, one scope down

`apply_envelopes` carries a guard added after Lamplight lost 4934 bytes of issue prose, and its comment states the rule exactly:

> **Against the DISK rather than against `self.canon`, and that is the whole point.** `self.canon` is what this write is derived from, so comparing to it can only ever agree with itself. The file is the thing that loses the prose, so the file is what gets asked.

**That is this guard, one scope up: compare the realisation against the disk before writing.**

### THE CHECK-FORM CORRECTED (laksa-dc), because the one first written here is a DEAD CHECK

This issue first specified the guard as *"refuse when it would write materially less than the tree had"*. **That is a size comparison and it is the wrong predicate.** The right one is:

> **the DISK carries files CANON DOES NOT MODEL**

**A realisation can be byte-LARGER and still drop `tasks.md`.** Size is a proxy that resembles the property and does not track it -- the same selector-resembles-the-population shape this estate has recorded repeatedly, authored here by the person filing the issue about it.

**AND THE CONTROL MATTERS AS MUCH AS THE PREDICATE:** a size-compare passes trivially on a minimal thread, so a clean run over such a thread proves nothing. **The guard needs a positive control over a thread that DOES carry unmodelled files.**

### Blast radius, measured read-only (laksa-dc)

**All 9 `NOT-STARTED` threads in that estate carry 3/3 of `design`/`impl`/`tasks`.** ST0106 was simply the first one STARTED since the behaviour arrived -- so this is systematic and latent, not a one-off. ST0107 (WIP, already at the canonical path) also carries 3/3 and is **deliberately unmeasured, because measuring means running a lifecycle verb on a live thread.**

Those nine are also the positive-control population the guard needs.

### The generated-view half NARROWS -- the 58 lines were a FORMAT CHANGE, not a loss

**Corrected by laksa-cc, measured across every thread in that repo.** The verblock, the change-control line and the AT-status-vocabulary block are **pre-v3 boilerplate the v3 renderer deliberately does not emit.** Every v3-active thread lacks them; ST0107 demonstrably lost the same blocks at its deliberate v3 migration with nothing lost; and v3's replacements are stronger.

So this issue's earlier claim -- *every pre-v3 thread carrying hand prose in acceptance.md has the same latent loss* -- **is withdrawn.** The generated-view SPLIT stands: prose in a generated view is at risk in principle. **What does not stand is treating this instance's prose as the thing at risk.** Any sweep narrows to thread-SPECIFIC prose, discriminated by diffing against the population's shared blocks.

**AND THE METHOD NOTE IS THE REUSABLE PART (laksa-cc):**

> **A diff of one artefact across a verb cannot tell a REGRESSION from a MIGRATION -- both look like content leaving. The discriminating comparison is against the POPULATION.**

That is why the original report read as loss and why the correction needed a different instrument rather than a closer look at the same one.

**It also makes this guard's fixture CLEANER:** with the prose-migration noise removed, the target is precisely *the disk carries FILES canon does not model*, and nothing else.

**This is the third instance in one day of the same class:** the estate documents a mechanism correctly and applies the fix one field short. `whiteboard-clock-guard.sh` (BSD's unspecified field, fixed for dates, left on HH:MM) and `0206` (compare-against-disk, scoped to an authored body, not to the record) are the other two. **All three were routed in from Laksa, from three unrelated directions.**

## Not claimed

That `st attach --from` CREATES an absent attachment row. It is verified many times over for updating a row that already exists; the absent-row case is unverified and should be proven on a throwaway thread before being used as the recovery route.

No claim about how many threads in any estate are in this partially-hydrated state. One was observed.
